reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Federal fund expenditure plans and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (7) and history note (L. 1972 H.B. 1477 § 2). Covers DNR's January submission of federal-fund expenditure plans for any year DNR desires to receive and expend federal funds in the next fiscal year to the senate and house appropriations committees and legislative research oversight division, plus seven minimum required plan elements and any additional committee-chair requests.

headings.title: Quarterly performance reports on federally funded programs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires DNR to submit detailed quarterly performance reports on each federally funded program to the committees after the next fiscal year begins.

headings.title: Limits on adding or expanding federal programs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Prohibits DNR from adding federal programs or expanding current federally funded programs beyond levels specified in legislature-approved plans.

headings.title: Legislative approval for multi-year federal programs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires programs continuing for more than one fiscal year to be submitted to the legislature for approval or rejection.

headings.title: Exclusion for federal funds not retained by department
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Excludes from sections 253.022 and 253.024 any federal funds of which DNR retains no part.

Confirmed all five drafted titles accurate and retained them.

headings.title: Director's authority to promulgate state park rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 230 § 1 through A.L. 1995 S.B. 3). Grants the DNR director permissive authority to make and promulgate reasonable rules and regulations necessary for maintaining, improving, acquiring, and preserving state parks.

headings.title: Rule filing and effectiveness under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers secretary-of-state filing and minimum ten-day effective period under chapter 536 for rules outside organization/internal management, plus the condition that chapter 253 rules are ineffective unless promulgated under section 536.024.

headings.title: Removal and punishment for park rule violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Subjects persons violating subsection 2 rules on visitor conduct or public use of park facilities to removal from a state park and other punishment as otherwise provided by law.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all three subsections and history note (through A.L. 1995 S.B. 3), and verified all fingerprints. Checked director rulemaking authority for state parks, chapter 536 filing and ten-day effective period alongside section 536.024 effectiveness for chapter 253 rules, and removal plus other lawful punishment for violating visitor-conduct or facility-use rules. headings.title: Park land acquisition, management, and gift deposits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1949 § 253.020, A.L. 1953 p. 317 § 3, A.L. 1961 p. 231). Covers DNR authority to acquire lands, rights, sites, objects, or facilities (including by purchase, lease, donation, agreement, or eminent domain), improve/operate/regulate them, and accept gifts or contributions, with monetary contributions deposited in the state park earnings fund exclusively for sections 253.010 to 253.100.

headings.title: Procedure for exercising eminent domain
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by specifying that when eminent domain is exercised, it follows the manner provided for the state highways and transportation commission.

Confirmed both drafted titles accurate and retained them.

headings.title: Display of MIA/POW and Honor and Remember flags
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 H.B. 1545, A.L. 2013 S.B. 106 merged with S.B. 117, A.L. 2018 S.B. 573). Directs DNR within state parks to accompany U.S. and Missouri flag displays with the MIA/POW flag and the Honor and Remember flag, subject to subsection 3 exemptions.

headings.title: Seeking donated POW/MIA flags from veterans' organizations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires DNR to contact local veterans' organizations for a donated flag if a state park lacks a POW/MIA flag (noting source uses 'POW/MIA' here versus 'MIA/POW' in subsection 1 and does not name the Honor and Remember flag in subsection 2).

headings.title: Exemptions for unavailable donations or flag policy conflicts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Exempts a state park from this section if unable to obtain a donated flag or if displaying the flag on the existing flagpole would conflict with Missouri's national and state flag-display policy.

headings.title: Park ranger certification, commission, and peace officer powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 230 § 2, A.L. 1983 H.B. 350). Covers chapter 590 certification, oath, state-park peace officer commission, and order-maintenance and arrest powers of park rangers and director-designated employees on DNR-controlled land and state and county highways within state park boundaries.

headings.title: Removal and disposal of abandoned vehicles or watercraft
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes park rangers to remove vehicles or watercraft left unattended for 48 hours (or sooner if creating a safety or health hazard) on park roads, land, or water under DNR supervision, following section 304.155 reporting, owner notification, and disposal procedures.

headings.title: Authorization to recruit, train, and accept volunteers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1995 S.B. 275, Effective 5-16-95). Authorizes the division of state parks to develop, recruit, train, and accept volunteer services supplementing department or division programs.

headings.title: Volunteer compliance with department and division rules and policies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Requires recruited, trained, or accepted volunteers to comply with applicable DNR and division rules and policies. Independent review revised title to include both applicable rules and policies of DNR and the division.

headings.title: Division duties for volunteer management and recognition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (6) and history/effective-date notes. Lists six mandatory division duties: staffing program management, developing citizen-involvement opportunities, providing written volunteer rules, educating volunteers on duties, maintaining a receptive environment, and recognizing exceptional service.

headings.title: Unpaid-employee status and legal expense fund protections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/effective-date notes. Deems volunteers unpaid employees accorded state legal expense fund and liability protections.

headings.title: Special-assignment expense reimbursement and state vehicle use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/effective-date notes. Covers permissive reimbursement from regular division appropriations for necessary expenses of volunteers on division-determined special assignments, and volunteer use of state vehicles under paid-staff rules.

headings.title: Definition of volunteer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history/effective-date notes. Defines 'volunteer' for section 253.067 as a person freely performing assigned division duties without monetary or material compensation.

headings.title: Termination of volunteer service by division director
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history/effective-date notes. Authorizes the division director to terminate any person's service as a volunteer.

headings.title: Annual publicly noticed district stakeholder meetings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 2013 H.B. 28 § 1 merged with H.B. 650 § 1; effective 8-28-13 for H.B. 28 and 10-11-13 for H.B. 650 after veto override). Requires the division of state parks to hold one annual stakeholder meeting in each park district upon public notice.

headings.title: Stakeholder petitions, director response timelines, and finality
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Allows a stakeholder to petition the state parks director on a policy or park issue previously presented to the facility manager and district supervisor; sets a 14-day response deadline, optional meeting, 30-day post-meeting written decision notice, and finality without review.

headings.title: Definition of stakeholder
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Defines 'stakeholder' for section 253.078 as a person interested in the petition's subject matter who has visited the park within the past sixty days.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all three subsections and all source notes (L. 2013 H.B. 28 § 1 merged with H.B. 650 § 1; dual effective dates 8-28-13 and 10-11-13 after H.B. 650 veto override), and verified all fingerprints. Checked annual district stakeholder meetings, prerequisite presentation to facility manager and district supervisor, 14-day response and 30-day post-meeting written notice timelines, non-reviewable finality, and the 60-day park-visit stakeholder definition. headings.title: Department operation of park facilities, fees, and funding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1953 p. 317 § 5 through A.L. 2019 S.B. 196), and 1951 case annotation. Covers the DNR director's permissive authority to construct and operate public services and facilities, charge reasonable fees, and construct facilities only with appropriated funds unless a donor agreement supplies nonstate support funding.

headings.title: Concession contract awards and private fee regulation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Authorizes the director to contract with private parties to construct and operate park facilities and services for up to 25 years with renewal option (subject to subsection 4's ten-year limit) and to supervise and regulate private operators' fees.

headings.title: Competitive sealed bidding, notice, and Missouri preference
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Covers competitive sealed bids for section contracts (except subsection 8 permits), sworn financial statements, public notice, newspaper advertising for $25,000+ expected gross receipts, accepting the most favorable responsible bid or rejecting for good cause, and preference for Missouri firms on comparable bids.

headings.title: Ten-year contract limit and improvement exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Prohibits contracts or renewals under subsection 2 exceeding ten years unless the director determines a longer term is needed for substantial capital or other improvements of sufficient value to the state.

headings.title: Contractor performance bond and escrow reserve alternative
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Requires a faithful-performance and legal-compliance bond from contractors, with an exception allowing a proportional cash reserve in an escrow account if the contractor states inability to provide a bond.

headings.title: Contractor recordkeeping, audits, and single-park contract limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes. Covers contractor receipt/disbursement records, biennial and contract-expiration DNR audits, and the rule for subsections 5 and 6 limiting a contract to one state park unless the director finds multi-park extension in the state's best interest.

headings.title: Restrictions on commercial park use and public-road exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7, history note, and 1951 annotation (State ex rel. Taylor v. Anderson, 362 Mo. 513, 242 S.W.2d 66, enjoining unauthorized park boat concessions under pre-1953 rules). Prohibits commercial sales, rentals, concessions, or commercial use of park property without written DNR permission or contract, excepting customary public-road transport of persons or vehicles including canoes.

headings.title: Commercial use permits without competitive bidding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and source notes. Authorizes the director to issue up to two-year commercial use permits without competitive sealed bids, exempt from concession-contract provisions unless expressly stated, limited to $100,000 annual gross receipts from in-park services involving only incidental use of park space or resources.

headings.title: Facility-head revolving funds for incidental expenses and refunds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1989 H.B. 613, A.L. 2002 S.B. 1015, A.L. 2011 H.B. 190). Covers warrants up to $1,500 per park or historic site payable to each facility head as a revolving fund for incidental expenses and public fee refunds, governed by commissioner of administration rules.

headings.title: Division director revolving fund for state park item sales
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by providing a warrant up to $500 to the director of the division of state parks as a revolving fund for cash transactions selling division-made items under commissioner of administration rules.

headings.title: State Park Earnings Fund creation, deposits, and authorized uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (5) and all source notes (L. 1953 p. 317 § 6 through A.L. 2013 H.B. 28 merged with H.B. 650; veto-override effective date 10-11-13 for H.B. 650; cross-reference to section 640.099 nonseverability clause). headings.title: Biennial nonreversion notwithstanding section 33.080

headings.title: Contractor performance and compliance bond requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Requires a good and sufficient faithful-performance and legal-compliance bond from all contractors.

headings.title: Contractor recordkeeping and state audit access
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Requires persons contracting with the state under this section to keep accurate receipt and disbursement records and allow audits by both DNR and the state auditor.

headings.title: Arrow Rock endowment fund creation, deposits, and bequest transfer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2002 S.B. 1015). Creates the DNR-administered Arrow Rock State Historic Site Endowment Fund, credits assets, earnings, and specified gifts, and transfers the $21,965.92 Bill and Cora Lee Miller bequest from the state park earnings fund.

headings.title: Exclusive use for Arrow Rock public interpretive programs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Restricts fund expenditures exclusively to enhancing Arrow Rock State Historic Site public interpretive programs, including exhibits, artifacts, publications, lecture fees, and similar interpretive needs.

headings.title: State treasurer custody and lawful investment of fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Designates the state treasurer as custodian of all moneys, bonds, securities, and rights credited to the fund and directs investment as provided by law.

headings.title: Annual interest expenditure limits before and after 2100
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Limits DNR annual spending to one-half of prior-fiscal-year earned interest until January 1, 2100, and permits spending up to full prior-fiscal-year earned interest beginning January 1, 2100.

headings.title: Appropriation requirement and reversion to endowment fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires general assembly appropriation for fund expenditures and returns unexpended fiscal-year appropriations to the Arrow Rock endowment fund notwithstanding section 33.080.

headings.title: Rock Island Trail endowment fund creation and deposits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2019 S.B. 196). headings.title: Exclusive corridor uses and section 253.090 transfer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Restricts fund use solely to operating, maintaining, developing, and securing DNR-owned, leased, or operated portions of the corridor east of milepost 215.325, and transfers prior deposits made for that purpose from the section 253.090 state park earnings fund.

headings.title: State treasurer custody and investment of fund assets
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Designates the state treasurer as custodian of moneys, bonds, securities, and rights in the fund and directs lawful investment.

headings.title: Appropriation requirement and nonreversion notwithstanding section 33.080
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires legislative appropriation for any expenditure, refund, or transfer from the fund and prevents biennial reversion to general revenue notwithstanding section 33.080.

headings.title: Conditional refunds or transfers if federal NITU is vacated
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. NITU if the U.S. Surface Transportation Board vacates the February 26, 2015 NITU in docket AB-1068 (Sub-No. 3X).

headings.title: Leash restraint rule and park building animal restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1971 H.B. 300 § 2, A.L. 2013 H.B. 28 merged with H.B. 650; H.B. 650 effective 10-11-13 after veto override). headings.title: Designation of state park dog parks or off-leash areas
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Grants DNR permissive authority to designate a specified area within any state park as a dog park or off-leash area for domestic household animals.

headings.title: Department authority to construct and operate park projects
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1957 p. 300 § 2). Authorizes DNR to acquire, construct, erect, equip, furnish, operate, control, manage, and regulate projects deemed necessary, advisable, and suitable for state parks and their facilities.

headings.title: Use of state park land and contiguous site acquisition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes DNR to site projects on existing state park real property or acquire real or personal property, subject to the exception that acquired real property project sites must be contiguous to and become part of a state park.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of both subsections and history note (L. 1957 p. 300 § 2), and verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Authority to issue and sell park project revenue bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1957 p. 300 § 3, A.L. 1961 p. 231). Authorizes DNR to issue and sell revenue bonds up to appropriations and estimated project and incidental costs for acquiring, constructing, equipping, furnishing, and siting a project.

headings.title: Approval prerequisites, revenue pledges, covenants, and reserve funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)(a)–(d) and (2)–(5) and history note. Conditions bond issuance on governor and general assembly approval, pledging net project revenues plus optional grant/park/other-project/concession revenues, covenanting sufficient user rates, and maintaining interest/sinking, reserve, and depreciation funds.

headings.title: Discretionary use of unencumbered park revenues for debt service
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes DNR in its discretion to apply unencumbered available project or park-contract net revenues—up to 50% of prior-year deposits to the 'department of natural resources earnings fund' (retaining exact archived fund name)—toward bond principal, interest, or sinking/reserve funds.

headings.title: Prohibition on bonds where private facilities are adequate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Bars issuing and selling revenue bonds if private facilities are adequate in the given park area.

headings.title: Deposit of bond proceeds into DNR Building Fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Creates the Department of Natural Resources Building Fund in the state treasury and directs deposit of bond sale proceeds into it.

headings.title: Denominations, interest cap, maturity limit, and bond types

headings.title: Optional early redemption and premium terms for serial bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Allows serial bonds to be issued with or without reserved early-redemption call rights, notice terms, and redemption premium covenants as DNR determines.

headings.title: Mandatory early redemption reservation for term bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 2 by requiring term bonds to reserve the right of prior-to-maturity call and redemption on notice and premium terms (if any) determined by DNR.

headings.title: Public sale notice and minimum ninety-five percent price

headings.title: Direct federal sales without public sale or notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Permits selling bonds directly to the United States or its agencies or instrumentalities at not less than par plus accrued interest without public sale or notice.

headings.title: Negotiability and state income tax exemption for interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Makes issued and sold bonds negotiable instruments and exempts bond interest from Missouri state income taxes.

headings.title: Bond form, details, incidents, and security covenants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1957 p. 300 § 7). Authorizes DNR to prescribe bond form, details, incidents, and security covenants not inconsistent with sections 253.210 to 253.280.

headings.title: Bondholder and coupon-holder suits to compel performance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. headings.title: Circumstances authorizing refunding and advance-refunding escrow
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and history note (L. 1957 p. 300 § 6, A.L. 1982 S.B. 696). headings.title: Issuance and allowable amount of refunding bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes DNR to issue refunding bonds (including to refund prior refunding bonds) in amounts needed to cover principal, unpaid/past-due interest, call premiums, and issuance costs.

headings.title: Manner of selling refunding bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires refunding bonds to be sold in the same manner as revenue bonds under sections 253.210 to 253.280.

headings.title: Use of proceeds, par exchange, maturity, and interest limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs refunding bond proceeds to pay/cancel old bonds, interest, and premiums (or par-value exchange), capped at 20-year maturity and 14% annual interest.

headings.title: Pledged revenue sources for paying refunding bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Allows refunding bonds to be payable from the same sources pledged to refunded bonds or, in DNR's discretion, any other source pledgeable under sections 253.210 to 253.280.

headings.title: Certificate issuance timing and supplemental excess-cost applications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and source notes. Sets certificate issuance in the final year of costs or within 12 months after rehabilitation concludes, and allows supplemental applications (subject to subsection 1 priority) when eligible costs exceed subsection 5 approval.

headings.title: Annual determination of statewide economic impact
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and source notes. Directs the department to determine annually the overall economic impact to the state from rehabilitating eligible property.

headings.title: Administrative appeals process and independent review panel
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 including subdivisions (1) through (9) and source notes. Establishes a non-adjudicative administrative appeal of DED or SHPO decisions before an uncompensated independent review panel and chair, with 30-day filing, 14-day agency notice, 30-day agency response, mandatory meeting right, and 90-day written decision.

headings.title: Retroactive application for applications from August 28, 2024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and source notes (including A.L. 2026 H.B. 3080). Makes sections 253.544 to 253.559 retroactive to all applications received or approved by the department on or after August 28, 2024. Independent review revised title to clarify that retroactive application of sections 253.544 to 253.559 governs applications received or approved on or after August 28, 2024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived text of all fourteen subsections (including all subdivisions and the continuation paragraph in subsection 2, block 17) and all source notes (through A.L. 2026 H.B. 3080 and Tax Credit Accountability Act cross-reference, sections 135.800 to 135.830), and verified all fingerprints. Checked year-round postmark/lottery priority, subsection 2 application contents and continuation single-property/disapproval/resubmission rules, fiscal/economic evaluation and exemptions, SHPO 60-day review/federal forwarding/phased 80%-20% credits, scope changes, taxpayer-identity exceptions, cap queueing, financing-capacity cure, 24-month commencement/rescission/forfeiture, final 75%/120-day issuance (retaining subsection 10(2)(b)'s exact source cross-reference to "subsection 3 of this section"), supplemental excess-cost applications, annual impact determination, non-adjudicative independent-panel appeals, and subsection 14 retroactivity to applications received or approved on or after August 28, 2024. Revised subsection 14 to clarify application-based retroactivity scope; retained subsections 1–13.
